_note: SAMPLE curated general guidance, not a personalized diet plan. Have a clinician/dietitian review before production use.

diabetes_type_2.label: Type 2 Diabetes
prefer: Whole grains (brown rice, whole wheat, millets/ragi)
High-fiber fruits in moderation (guava, apple, berries)
diabetes_type_2.notes: Consistent meal timing and portion control matter as much as food choice. Pair carbohydrates with protein/fiber to slow glucose spikes.

diabetes_type_1.label: Type 1 Diabetes
prefer: Consistent carbohydrate counting to match insulin dosing
avoid: Skipping meals after taking insulin (hypoglycemia risk)
Large unplanned sugar intake without adjusting insulin
diabetes_type_1.notes: Diet must be coordinated with insulin dosing and timing — work with your endocrinologist/dietitian on carbohydrate counting.

hypertension.label: Hypertension (High Blood Pressure)
prefer: Fruits and vegetables (potassium-rich: banana, spinach, sweet potato)
hypertension.notes: The DASH-style eating pattern (low sodium, high potassium/fiber) is well supported for blood pressure control.

dyslipidemia.label: High Cholesterol
dyslipidemia.notes: Combine with regular physical activity; medication and diet work together, not as substitutes for each other.

hypothyroidism.label: Hypothyroidism
prefer: Iodine-adequate diet (iodized salt) unless otherwise advised
avoid: Taking levothyroxine with calcium/iron supplements or high-fiber meals at the same time (reduces absorption — separate by hours)
Excessive raw cruciferous vegetables (cabbage, soy) right around dosing time in very large amounts
hypothyroidism.notes: Take levothyroxine on an empty stomach, consistently timed, separate from food and interacting supplements — timing matters more than any single food.

ckd.label: Chronic Kidney Disease
prefer: Portion-controlled protein as advised by your nephrologist
Fresh, home-cooked food with controlled salt
avoid: High-potassium foods in advanced stages (banana, coconut water, tomato) — only if your doctor says your potassium is high
ckd.notes: CKD diet needs are highly individual and stage-dependent — this is general orientation only; follow your nephrologist/renal dietitian's specific plan.

asthma.label: Asthma
avoid: Known personal food triggers (vary by individual — e.g. sulfites in some dried fruits/wine for sensitive people)
asthma.notes: Diet plays a smaller role than trigger avoidance (allergens, smoke, cold air) and correct inhaler technique/adherence.
